provenance: R 4.6.1, package pdR 1.9.4 (SMPLSplit_het, encapsulating B. E. Hansen's own code for Hansen 2000, Econometrica), executed via validation/external/spec32_pdR.R on tests/replication/data/spec32_synthetic.csv (n=300, seed=32, known threshold at q=0). Raw R output: validation/results/external_logs/spec32_pdR.log. Numeric capture: validation/external/spec32_pdR.json.
notes: gamma_hat matches to the precision R prints (-0.02553838 vs pyardl's -0.0255383810909059) — a tight, direct check of the core grid-search SSR-minimisation, the part of the algorithm shared with any implementation. The test statistics are NOT expected to match: pdR::SMPLSplit_het computes a heteroskedasticity-robust (White-corrected) LM statistic by construction (the function name says so), while pyardl's linearity_stat is a classical homoskedastic F-statistic — two different, both legitimate, functional forms, not a numerical discrepancy to chase. Both reject H0 overwhelmingly on this DGP, which is the only comparison that is meaningful across the two statistics.
